set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A patient with chronic urticaria is still symptomatic on a standard dose of a non-sedating antihistamine. What comes next?
opts: Increase to up to four times the standard dose, and consider adding an H2 blocker
Correct — omalizumab and ciclosporin follow if that fails.
Switch immediately to a long-term oral corticosteroid taken daily
Long-term systemic steroid is not the described escalation.
Switch across to a first-generation sedating antihistamine at standard dose
The escalation is in dose of the non-sedating agent, not a switch back.
Stop the antihistamine and start a leukotriene antagonist alone
Stopping the antihistamine is not the described step.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which features separate a fixed drug eruption from erythema multiforme?
opts: It produces wheals that migrate, blanch fully and resolve within twenty-four hours of first appearing
That describes urticaria.
It produces extensive epidermal detachment with mucosal involvement and systemic toxicity
That describes Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
It produces tender nodules on the anterior shins that never go on to ulcerate
That describes erythema nodosum.
It recurs at the same site, leaves residual hyperpigmentation, and has few lesions without three concentric zones
Correct — the three-zone target is what defines an erythema multiforme lesion.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which drug classes are classic causes of phototoxicity?
opts: Aromatic anticonvulsants, allopurinol and nevirapine
Those are the leading triggers of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Oral contraceptives, sulfonamides and bromides
Those are drug triggers of erythema nodosum.
Tetracyclines, fluoroquinolones, amiodarone and thiazides
Correct, alongside furosemide, voriconazole, some nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and psoralens.
Sunscreen chemicals, sulfonamides and phenothiazines
Those are the classic photoallergens rather than phototoxic agents.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the main differential for localised granuloma annulare, and how is it separated?
opts: Rheumatoid nodules, which are firm, periarticular and serology positive
These are a differential chiefly for the subcutaneous variant.
Lichen planus, which is violaceous and polygonal with Wickham striae
This is a listed differential but not the principal one.
Tinea corporis, which has a scaling border and is potassium hydroxide positive
Correct — granuloma annulare has no scale on its ring.
Necrobiosis lipoidica, which has a yellow-waxy atrophic centre on the shins
This is a differential but is distinguished by its site and appearance rather than being the main one.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How is a positive photopatch test interpreted?
opts: Any reaction indicates phototoxicity regardless of which patch responds
The test is designed specifically to separate photoallergy from contact allergy.
A reaction only on the irradiated patch indicates photoallergy; a reaction on both indicates contact allergy
Correct — the suspected photohaptens are applied in duplicate and one set irradiated with ultraviolet A.
A reaction on both patches indicates photoallergy; a reaction on one indicates phototoxicity
Reaction on both patches indicates ordinary contact allergy.
A reaction on the non-irradiated patch alone indicates photoallergy
That result would indicate contact allergy independent of light.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is beremagene geperpavec?
opts: A non-adherent biological dressing designed for fragile skin
Mepitel and Mepilex are the dressings described; this is a gene therapy.
A topical gene therapy gel approved in 2023 for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa
Correct, accessible through dermatology referral centres and gene therapy trials.
A monoclonal antibody given intravenously for junctional epidermolysis bullosa
It is a topical gene therapy rather than an antibody.
An oral small molecule that restores keratin 5 and 14 function
It is a topical gel and does not act on keratin genes.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which systemic complications are named in toxic epidermal necrolysis?
opts: Acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, acute rheumatic fever and a post-infectious reactive arthritis of the knee
Those follow streptococcal infection.
Neurocutaneous melanosis, hydrocephalus and seizures in early childhood
Those belong to large congenital melanocytic naevi.
Symblepharon alone, with no involvement of any other organ system
Ocular scarring is one complication among many.
Sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury, electrolyte imbalance, hypovolaemia and gastrointestinal haemorrhage
Correct — survivors also face sicca syndrome, lung disease and psychological trauma.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the role of sub-antimicrobial dose doxycycline in rosacea?
opts: It reduces flushing by blocking alpha-adrenergic receptors in the skin
That is the mechanism of brimonidine and oxymetazoline.
It prevents rhinophyma from developing in male patients
Rhinophyma is managed with isotretinoin, laser or surgery.
It is approved for papulopustular rosacea and works as an anti-inflammatory rather than an antimicrobial
Correct, at 40 mg modified-release daily.
It eradicates Demodex folliculorum from the follicles over the course of several weeks of therapy
Ivermectin targets Demodex; doxycycline at this dose acts on inflammation.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A patient has had four episodes of herpes-associated erythema multiforme this year. Which chronic measure is appropriate?
opts: Annual phototherapy given as a five-week course each spring
That is preventive therapy for polymorphous light eruption.
Suppressive antiviral therapy, such as aciclovir 400 mg twice daily
Correct — preventing the herpes recurrence prevents the eruption.
A standing prescription for oral prednisone to take at each episode
Steroid at each episode does not prevent recurrence.
Long-term oral antihistamines taken continuously through the year
Antihistamines address pruritus rather than recurrence.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What causes phytophotodermatitis, and how does it present?
opts: Furanocoumarins in plants such as lime, celery and parsley plus ultraviolet A, producing linear streaked hyperpigmentation
Correct — classically after lime juice and sun exposure, with painful blistering acutely.
Bergapten in bergamot oil used in fragrances and cosmetics, producing drip-pattern hyperpigmentation of the neck
That describes berloque dermatitis, a separate subtype.
A persistent eczematous eruption in chronically exposed skin of older males
That describes chronic actinic dermatitis.
A delayed hypersensitivity response to an ultraviolet-induced photoantigen
That describes polymorphous light eruption.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which investigation is the gold standard for epidermolysis bullosa?
opts: Transmission electron microscopy with immunofluorescence antigen mapping
Correct — a genetic panel and nutritional labs support it.
Perilesional direct immunofluorescence looking for granular immunoglobulin A
That establishes dermatitis herpetiformis.
Punch biopsy showing full-thickness epidermal necrosis of the specimen
That is Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
Serum enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for anti-desmoglein antibodies
That supports pemphigus.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which single intervention most improves survival in Stevens-Johnson syndrome?
opts: Immediate withdrawal of the causative drug, since each day of delay worsens prognosis
Correct — earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival.
Early administration of intravenous immunoglobulin at 1 g/kg daily for three days
This shows benefit in retrospective studies but is not the intervention with the strongest survival link.
Prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics started on admission
Antibiotic prophylaxis is explicitly not recommended; infections are treated when confirmed.
High-dose systemic corticosteroids given throughout the admission
Systemic corticosteroids remain controversial and are avoided in active infection.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which biologic is approved for refractory chronic urticaria?
opts: Omalizumab, an anti-immunoglobulin E antibody given every four weeks
Correct, at 300 mg subcutaneously.
Infliximab, a tumour necrosis factor alpha inhibitor given intravenously
Infliximab is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease.
Dupilumab, an interleukin-4 receptor antagonist given subcutaneously
Dupilumab has been reported in refractory granuloma annulare rather than approved here.
Etanercept, a tumour necrosis factor inhibitor given subcutaneously
Etanercept is described as an emerging adjunct in Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which topical agent is the only one approved for photoaging, and how does it work?
opts: Niacinamide, which reduces inflammation and improves skin sallowness
Niacinamide is an adjunct rather than the approved agent.
Tretinoin, which stimulates collagen synthesis and inhibits matrix metalloproteinase activity
Correct, requiring a minimum of six to twelve months for visible results.
Hydroquinone, which inhibits melanin production within the epidermis
Hydroquinone treats hyperpigmentation but is not the approved photoaging agent.
Vitamin C, which neutralises reactive oxygen species and stimulates new collagen
Vitamin C is an adjunct antioxidant rather than the approved agent.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which pyoderma gangrenosum variant is most often associated with haematologic malignancy?
opts: The bullous variant, with tense superficial bullae and blue-grey overhanging edges on the upper limbs and face
Correct — acute myeloid leukaemia is the named association.
The classic ulcerative variant, with an undermined violaceous border on the lower extremities only
That is the commonest form and associates with inflammatory bowel disease.
The pustular variant, with painful discrete pustules arising on inflamed skin
That variant is not the one tied to haematologic malignancy.
The vegetative variant, with a slowly enlarging superficial verrucous plaque
That variant is not the one tied to haematologic malignancy.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is first-line treatment for acute urticaria?
opts: Intramuscular epinephrine at 0.3 mg given immediately on presentation
That is for anaphylaxis rather than for uncomplicated urticaria.
Omalizumab 300 mg subcutaneously repeated every four weeks
That is for refractory chronic disease.
A first-generation sedating antihistamine taken four times daily
Second-generation non-sedating agents are first line.
A second-generation antihistamine such as cetirizine, loratadine or fexofenadine
Correct — a short prednisone course is added for severe acute disease.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is used for suppressive therapy in recurrent herpes-associated erythema multiforme?
opts: Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily taken indefinitely
Hydroxychloroquine is also reserved for refractory non-herpes recurrent disease.
Prednisone 40 to 60 mg daily for five days at each recurrence
A short steroid course is used in some acute settings rather than as suppression.
Acyclovir 400 mg twice daily or valacyclovir 500 mg daily
Correct. Dapsone or hydroxychloroquine are used for refractory non-herpes recurrent disease.
Dapsone 25 to 200 mg daily with regular monitoring of the blood count
Dapsone is reserved for refractory recurrent disease that is not herpes-associated.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which group carries markedly increased actinic keratosis risk?
opts: Patients with coeliac disease, at roughly 30 times the risk
That association belongs to dermatitis herpetiformis.
Organ transplant recipients, at roughly 65 times the risk
Correct, alongside Fitzpatrick types I and II, male sex, age over fifty and outdoor occupation.
Patients with atopic dermatitis, at roughly 20 times the risk
Atopy is not among the named risk factors.
Patients with inflammatory bowel disease, at roughly 10 times the risk
That association belongs to pyoderma gangrenosum.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which features suggest malignant rather than benign acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Gradual onset over years confined to the posterior neck and axillae
That is the pattern of the common insulin-resistant form.
Velvety hyperpigmented plaques appearing only in the inframammary folds
Fold involvement is typical of the benign form.
Lesions that wipe away completely with an isopropyl alcohol swab
That describes terra firma-forme dermatosis, a differential.
Rapid onset, extensive involvement, oral mucosal change and tripe palms
Correct — malignant disease is paraneoplastic, especially with gastric adenocarcinoma.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which features in an actinic keratosis are described as concerning?
opts: A sandpaper texture on palpation of the lesion
That is the ordinary description of the lesion.
A diameter between two and ten millimetres
That is the typical size range.
A skin-coloured to red-brown appearance overall
That is the typical colour range.
Pruritus, tenderness and bleeding
Correct — a hypertrophic, thickened and verrucous lesion also carries higher malignant potential.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which single feature most usefully distinguishes erythema nodosum from nodular vasculitis?
opts: Erythema nodosum nodules are painless on palpation
The nodules are tender, which is part of the classic description.
Erythema nodosum nodules occur exclusively in men
There is a female predominance of three to six to one.
Erythema nodosum nodules do not ulcerate
Correct, and they sit on the anterior shins whereas nodular vasculitis favours the posterior legs and ulcerates.
Erythema nodosum nodules appear only on the posterior legs
The anterior shins are the characteristic site.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What does the lecture say about patients with Fitzpatrick types IV to VI?
opts: They are not immune to ultraviolet damage or skin cancer, and melanoma is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages
Correct — delayed diagnosis is common because of a lower index of suspicion.
They carry no meaningful skin cancer risk and need no routine photoprotection
Risk is lower but explicitly not absent.
They burn more readily than types I to III but tan more deeply afterwards
Types IV to VI burn minimally or never.
They should use SPF 15 rather than SPF 30, on the basis that higher factors confer no additional benefit
The guidance is broad-spectrum SPF 30 or above for daily use across all types.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which advice is given about blisters in second-degree sunburn?
opts: Apply a high-potency topical corticosteroid directly to them
Topical steroids have limited evidence and may help only within six hours.
Cover them with silver sulfadiazine to prevent colonisation
That agent is specifically avoided in severe cutaneous drug reactions.
Do not pop them, because intact blisters are protective
Correct, with cool compresses and early nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for pain.
Drain them under sterile conditions to reduce infection risk
Intact blisters protect the underlying skin.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the cornerstone of long-term management in dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Sulfapyridine taken indefinitely in place of dietary change
Sulfapyridine is an alternative for patients intolerant of dapsone.
A strict lifelong gluten-free diet
Correct, and it may allow dapsone to be reduced or stopped over one to two years.
Indefinite daily dapsone at the lowest effective dose
Dapsone gives rapid relief but the diet is the long-term cornerstone.
Long-term high-potency topical corticosteroids to affected sites
Topical steroids are used for localised flares only.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which features should raise suspicion of secondary rather than primary hyperhidrosis?
opts: Sweating confined to the axillae with a family history of the same
That pattern describes primary focal disease.
Generalised sweating, nocturnal sweating, or an asymmetric distribution
Correct — primary disease is bilateral, focal and absent during sleep.
Bilateral palmar sweating that has been present since adolescence
That pattern describes primary focal disease.
Sweating that worsens with anxiety and improves in a cool room
Anxiety exacerbates primary disease without indicating a secondary cause.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What kind of process is erythema nodosum, histologically?
opts: A lobular panniculitis with associated vasculitis
That describes nodular vasculitis, or erythema induratum, a differential.
A palisading granuloma around degenerating collagen
That describes granuloma annulare.
A dense neutrophilic infiltrate without organisms
That describes pyoderma gangrenosum.
A septal panniculitis without vasculitis
Correct — the most common form of panniculitis, a delayed hypersensitivity reaction in subcutaneous fat.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which referrals are named for erythema nodosum, and what determines each?
opts: Pulmonology or rheumatology for Löfgren syndrome, gastroenterology for inflammatory bowel disease, infectious diseases for tuberculosis or endemic mycoses, dermatology for atypical cases
Correct — the referral follows the suspected underlying cause.
Dermatology in every single case, since the diagnosis requires a deep incisional biopsy taken from one of the affected nodules before any treatment at all begins
Biopsy is reserved for atypical presentations.
Vascular surgery in every case, since the nodules reflect venous disease
Erythema nodosum is a panniculitis rather than a venous condition.
Oncology in every case, since the condition is usually paraneoplastic
Malignancy is not the leading association here.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which haplotypes are strongly associated with dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: HLA-Cw6 and HLA-B27
Those are associated with psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.
HLA-A31 and HLA-BW35
Those are the suggested susceptibility haplotypes for granuloma annulare.
HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8
Correct, and nearly all patients have underlying gluten-sensitive enteropathy even when gastrointestinally asymptomatic.
HLA-B*15:02 and HLA-B*58:01
Those are the pharmacogenomic risk alleles for Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the hardening phenomenon in polymorphous light eruption?
opts: Loss of pigment in the affected areas after each episode
This is not a described feature.
Improvement through the summer as tolerance develops after repeated exposure
Correct, which is also why prophylactic narrowband ultraviolet B in spring is the most effective preventive strategy.
Thickening and hardening of the skin from repeated scratching of the eruption
That describes lichenification.
Progressive scarring of affected sites over successive seasons
The eruption resolves without scarring.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which biologic is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease?
opts: Omalizumab at 300 mg subcutaneously every four weeks
That is approved for refractory chronic urticaria.
Etanercept at 25 to 50 mg subcutaneously
That is described as an emerging adjunct in Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
Dupilumab given subcutaneously every two weeks
That has been reported in refractory granuloma annulare.
Infliximab at 5 mg/kg intravenously
Correct — the biologic of choice in that setting, with adalimumab and ustekinumab for refractory cases.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which is the central education point for a patient with erythema nodosum?
opts: It is a reaction pattern rather than an isolated disease, so identifying and treating the trigger is the point
Correct — that is why the workup matters as much as the symptomatic care.
It is an infection of the subcutaneous fat that requires a prolonged course of oral antibiotics
It is a delayed hypersensitivity reaction rather than an infection.
It is a chronic condition that will require lifelong immunosuppressive therapy
Most cases settle once the trigger is addressed.
It is a premalignant change that requires excision of the affected nodules
The nodules are benign and are not excised.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which referral is named for palmar hyperhidrosis refractory to all other treatments?
opts: Endocrinology, for assessment of thyroid and adrenal function
That referral addresses secondary hyperhidrosis.
Psychiatry, since refractory palmar sweating is usually anxiety-driven
Anxiety exacerbates but does not cause primary disease.
Thoracic surgery, for endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy
Correct — dermatology handles botulinum toxin, microwave thermolysis and glycopyrronium.
Dermatology, for a further trial of topical aluminium chloride
That is the first-line therapy that has already failed.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What must be checked before starting dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Serum immunoglobulin A level to exclude selective deficiency
This affects serological interpretation rather than dapsone safety.
HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 typing to confirm susceptibility
Typing is used when serology is equivocal rather than before dapsone.
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase status
Correct, and the blood count is then monitored for haemolytic anaemia and methaemoglobinaemia.
Thyroid-stimulating hormone and anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies
Autoimmune thyroid disease is an association but is not the pre-treatment check.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What does biopsy show in granuloma annulare?
opts: Palisading granulomas with central necrobiosis and mucin deposition
Correct — thought to involve a type IV delayed hypersensitivity reaction around degenerating collagen.
Septal panniculitis without vasculitis and Miescher's granulomas
That is erythema nodosum.
A dense neutrophilic infiltrate at the ulcer edge
That is pyoderma gangrenosum.
Interface dermatitis with scattered necrotic keratinocytes
That is erythema multiforme.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the gold standard test for determining the cleavage plane in epidermolysis bullosa?
opts: Serum enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for structural protein antibodies
Inherited epidermolysis bullosa is not antibody-mediated.
Skin biopsy with transmission electron microscopy
Correct, with immunofluorescence antigen mapping used to localise missing or reduced proteins.
Skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence for immunoglobulin G
That distinguishes acquired autoimmune blistering disease rather than mapping the cleavage plane.
Genetic testing of the known structural protein genes
Genetic testing is confirmatory and guides prognosis and counselling.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which organism contributes to papulopustular rosacea?
opts: Demodex folliculorum, whose overgrowth drives inflammation
Correct, which is why ivermectin 1% cream outperforms metronidazole in Demodex-associated disease.
Malassezia, whose overgrowth drives inflammation in sebum-rich areas
Malassezia drives seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Staphylococcus aureus, colonising the follicles
This organism is not implicated in rosacea.
Cutibacterium acnes, proliferating within blocked follicles
That organism relates to acne vulgaris.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which risk factors are named for erythema multiforme?
opts: Recurrent herpes simplex infection, immunosuppression, high-risk medications, recent respiratory infection and a prior episode
Correct — a prior episode itself carries recurrence risk.
Chronic venous insufficiency, obesity, immobility, previous deep vein thrombosis and chronic lower-limb oedema
Those are the risk factors for stasis dermatitis in Lecture 2.
Cumulative ultraviolet exposure, fair skin, outdoor work, immunosuppression and older age
Those are the risk factors for actinic damage.
Nasal staphylococcal carriage, obesity, diabetes, occlusive clothing and humid weather
Those are the risk factors for folliculitis in Lecture 4.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How is the diagnosis of pyoderma gangrenosum established?
opts: By wound culture growing a characteristic organism
Cultures are obtained to exclude an infectious cause; they are negative in pyoderma gangrenosum.
By serum antibody testing against dermal structural proteins
The condition is not antibody-mediated in that way.
By exclusion, since there is no gold standard test
Correct — biopsy from the ulcer edge shows dense neutrophils and rules out malignancy and infection.
By biopsy showing a pathognomonic palisading granuloma
Palisading granulomas belong to granuloma annulare.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What distinguishes phototoxicity from photoallergy?
opts: Phototoxicity is non-immunologic and dose-dependent and occurs on first exposure; photoallergy is immunologic and dose-independent and requires prior sensitisation
Correct — phototoxicity resembles an exaggerated sunburn within hours.
Phototoxicity is immunologic and requires prior sensitisation before any reaction; photoallergy is non-immunologic, dose-dependent and occurs on the very first exposure
The mechanisms are reversed.
Phototoxicity affects only sun-exposed skin; photoallergy affects only covered skin
Photoallergy characteristically extends beyond sun-exposed skin.
Phototoxicity resolves on stopping the drug; photoallergy always resolves immediately too
Photoallergy can persist after the drug is stopped, as a persistent light reaction.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What distinguishes solar lentigo from lentigo maligna?
opts: Solar lentigo has uniform pigmentation; lentigo maligna is asymmetric with irregular border and colour
Correct, and dermoscopy is essential — solar lentigo shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border.
Solar lentigo is raised and rough; lentigo maligna is flat and smooth
Solar lentigo is a macule without induration or scale.
Solar lentigo appears in early childhood; lentigo maligna appears only after the age of seventy
Solar lentigo reflects cumulative exposure, exceeding 90% prevalence in Caucasians over seventy.
Solar lentigo appears on covered skin; lentigo maligna on exposed skin
Solar lentigo occurs on chronically sun-exposed surfaces.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is first-line systemic therapy for acute rapidly progressive pyoderma gangrenosum?
opts: Dapsone at 100 mg daily by mouth
That is not the described first-line systemic agent.
Doxycycline at 100 mg twice daily
Antibiotics do not treat this neutrophilic dermatosis.
Prednisone at 0.5 to 1 mg/kg daily
Correct — ciclosporin at 3 to 5 mg/kg daily is the alternative.
Infliximab at 5 mg/kg intravenously
That is used in inflammatory bowel disease-associated and refractory disease.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which referral is named when squamous or basal cell carcinoma is confirmed in a photoaged patient?
opts: Plastic surgery, for advanced cosmetic restoration
That referral is for cosmetic rather than oncological work.
Genetics, for suspected DNA repair disorder assessment
That referral applies to premature photoaging suggesting xeroderma pigmentosum.
Rheumatology, for the connective tissue changes of solar elastosis
Solar elastosis is not managed by rheumatology.
Dermatologic surgery, including Mohs surgery
Correct — oncology handles melanoma and advanced squamous cell carcinoma.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What drives the commonest, insulin-resistant form of acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Hyperinsulinaemia stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation
Correct. Malignant, drug-induced and endocrine forms make up the rest.
Autoimmune destruction of the melanocytes within the affected intertriginous skin
That is vitiligo.
Chronic ultraviolet exposure driving proliferation of the basal layer melanocytes and increased melanin production
That is solar lentigo.
Immunoglobulin A deposition in the dermal papillae activating neutrophils
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the underlying mechanism of dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Immunoglobulin E mediated mast cell degranulation with histamine release
That mechanism produces urticaria.
Immunoglobulin A antibodies against epidermal transglutaminase, depositing in the dermal papillae
Correct, in genetically susceptible individuals consuming gluten, producing subepidermal blisters.
Immunoglobulin G antibodies directed against the epithelial basement membrane zone of the skin
That mechanism produces bullous pemphigoid.
Immunoglobulin G antibodies against keratinocyte adhesion molecules
That mechanism produces pemphigus.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How much do tanning beds reduce risk compared with natural sun, and how are they classified?
opts: They halve ultraviolet B exposure while delivering the same ultraviolet A dose
No such reduction is described; they are classified as carcinogenic.
They are safer for Fitzpatrick types I and II under supervision
Those types carry the highest risk from any ultraviolet exposure.
They are acceptable if limited to the months outside peak summer
No safe level of tanning is described.
They are not safer at all, and are classified as Group 1 carcinogens
Correct — there is no safe level of tanning.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the immunological basis of dermatitis herpetiformis?
opts: Immunoglobulin G antibodies against desmoglein between the keratinocytes
That is pemphigus vulgaris.
A T-cell mediated destruction of melanocytes within the affected epidermis
That is vitiligo.
Immunoglobulin A antibodies against epidermal transglutaminase, forming complexes that deposit in the dermal papillae
Correct — complement and neutrophils are then activated, producing subepidermal blisters.
Immunoglobulin G antibodies directed against the epidermal basement membrane zone at the dermal junction
That is bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What mechanism underlies the most common form of acanthosis nigricans?
opts: Autoantibody deposition along the epithelial basement membrane zone
That mechanism produces bullous pemphigoid.
Hyperinsulinaemia stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation through insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor cross-activation
Correct — the insulin-resistant or benign form is the commonest.
A paraneoplastic process driven by an underlying gastric adenocarcinoma secreting growth factors that act on the epidermis
Malignant acanthosis nigricans is rare, at under 1% of cases.
A delayed type IV hypersensitivity reaction to a contacted allergen
That mechanism produces allergic contact dermatitis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What does direct immunofluorescence show in erythema multiforme, and why does it matter?
opts: It shows intercellular immunoglobulin G throughout the epidermis, confirming the diagnosis
That pattern indicates pemphigus.
It is negative, which distinguishes erythema multiforme from pemphigoid and pemphigus
Correct. Biopsy shows interface dermatitis with vacuolar degeneration of the basal layer and necrotic keratinocytes.
It shows granular immunoglobulin A in the dermal papillae, confirming the diagnosis
That finding is the gold standard for dermatitis herpetiformis instead.
It shows linear immunoglobulin G at the basement membrane zone, confirming the diagnosis
That pattern indicates bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What triggers the majority of erythema multiforme cases?
opts: Sulfonamide antibiotics, accounting for over 50% of cases
Drugs including sulfonamides are triggers, but they are far from the majority.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae, accounting for over 50% of cases
Mycoplasma is a recognised infectious trigger but not the leading one.
Idiopathic causes, accounting for over 50% of cases
Idiopathic causes account for roughly 10% of cases.
Herpes simplex virus, accounting for over 50% of cases
Correct. Other infectious causes include Mycoplasma pneumoniae, histoplasmosis, Epstein-Barr virus and coxsackievirus.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which rosacea subtype is most common, and what defines it?
opts: Ocular, with blepharitis, conjunctivitis and meibomian gland dysfunction
This may precede or follow the skin findings but is not the most common subtype.
Erythematotelangiectatic, with persistent central facial erythema, flushing and telangiectasias but no papules or pustules
Correct — the skin is often described as sensitive and stinging.
Papulopustular, with transient central facial papules and pustules on a background of erythema and no comedones
This is the classic presentation but not the most common subtype.
Phymatous, with skin thickening and nodular enlargement of the nose and chin
This predominates in males but is not the most common subtype.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which type of epidermolysis bullosa is most common, and what is its cleavage level?
opts: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with cleavage in the lamina lucida
Junctional disease carries the highest mortality but is not the commonest.
Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with sub-lamina densa cleavage
Dystrophic disease arises from COL7A1 mutations but is not the commonest.
Kindler epidermolysis bullosa, at about 70% of cases, with mixed cleavage planes
Kindler disease is rare and arises from FERMT1 mutation.
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex, at about 70% of cases, with intraepidermal cleavage
Correct — it results from keratin 5 and 14 mutations and is autosomal dominant.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How is an isolated actinic keratosis usually treated?
opts: Imiquimod applied twice weekly for sixteen weeks
That is also field-directed rather than lesion-directed.
Photodynamic therapy using aminolevulinic acid and light
This is excellent for field treatment rather than an isolated lesion.
Cryotherapy with two to three freeze-thaw cycles
Correct — the standard of care for isolated lesions, with shave excision or curettage as alternatives.
5-fluorouracil cream applied for two to four weeks
That is a field-directed treatment for multiple or confluent lesions.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which biopsy finding is described as pathognomonic across the Stevens-Johnson and toxic epidermal necrolysis spectrum?
opts: Septal panniculitis without any accompanying vasculitis
That is erythema nodosum.
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with dermal-epidermal junction separation
Correct, on punch biopsy.
Granular immunoglobulin A deposited within the dermal papillae of the skin
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.
Palisading granulomas surrounding an area of necrobiosis
That is granuloma annulare.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which feature separates photodermatitis from seborrhoeic dermatitis on the face?
opts: Photodermatitis produces greasy yellow scale, which seborrhoeic dermatitis lacks
Greasy yellow scale is the seborrhoeic finding.
Photodermatitis is confined to the scalp, which seborrhoeic dermatitis spares
Neither statement is correct.
Photodermatitis spares the nasolabial folds, which seborrhoeic dermatitis involves
Correct — shadowed areas are protected from light.
Photodermatitis involves the nasolabial folds, which seborrhoeic dermatitis spares
That reverses the two.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What does skin biopsy show in polymorphous light eruption, and how useful is it?
opts: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with dermal-epidermal separation — pathognomonic
That is Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
Granular immunoglobulin A at the dermal papillae — diagnostic in every case
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.
Solar elastosis with tangled elastin fibres — the defining histological change
That is dermatoheliosis.
A perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate with dermal oedema — supportive but not pathognomonic
Correct. The diagnosis is largely clinical, from history and morphology.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How are acute and chronic urticaria distinguished?
opts: By severity — chronic urticaria involves more of the body surface
Extent of involvement is not what defines the split.
By trigger — chronic urticaria always has an identifiable cause
Over half of chronic cases have no identifiable trigger.
By age — chronic urticaria occurs only in adults over forty
Age is not what defines the split.
By duration — chronic urticaria has persisted beyond six weeks
Correct. Both are mast cell-mediated, with transient pruritic wheals.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the time course of sunburn after exposure?
opts: Onset within minutes of exposure, peaking within the first hour
That immediate timing suggests solar urticaria instead.
Onset thirty minutes to hours after exposure, resolving in seven to ten days
That timing describes polymorphous light eruption.
Onset two to three days after exposure, peaking at one week
Onset is considerably faster than this.
Onset three to five hours after exposure, peaking at twelve to twenty-four hours
Correct — which is why the injury is often underestimated at the time.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which test is mandatory when investigating polymorphous light eruption?
opts: Skin biopsy, which shows a pathognomonic pattern
Biopsy is supportive rather than pathognomonic.
An antinuclear antibody panel, to exclude lupus erythematosus
Correct, especially anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB.
A porphyrin screen of urine, stool and red cells in every patient
That is done only if erythropoietic protoporphyria is suspected.
Photopatch testing with the standard photoallergen series
That is used when photoallergic contact dermatitis is suspected.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the most common infectious trigger of erythema nodosum?
opts: Group A Streptococcus
Correct, alongside Yersinia, tuberculosis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis and hepatitis B and C.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae
Mycoplasma is a leading trigger of erythema multiforme rather than erythema nodosum.
Herpes simplex virus
Herpes simplex triggers over half of erythema multiforme cases.
Staphylococcus aureus
This organism is not among the named triggers.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How does polymorphous light eruption typically present?
opts: Persistent eczematous change in chronically exposed skin of older males
That describes chronic actinic dermatitis.
Papules appearing thirty minutes to hours after exposure on the décolletage, forearms and dorsal hands, sparing chronically exposed skin
Correct, resolving in seven to ten days without scarring and recurring each spring.
Painful erythema developing within minutes of ultraviolet exposure and resolving within an hour of moving into the shade
That immediate pattern suggests solar urticaria.
An exaggerated sunburn on first exposure to a new medication
That describes phototoxicity.
